numerical_failure.expected_behavior: solve_power should return nan when it fails to converge (success flag is 0), signalling no solution was found; cases that currently converge are unchanged.

category_specific_evidence: Root finder fails to converge when the power equation has no solution (e.g. one-sided test with effect_size pointing into the wrong tail), and solve_power returned the last evaluated point (a bracket bound such as 10 / array([10.])) as if it were a valid sample size.

Fix sets val = np.nan when the root finder did not converge, keyed off the existing success flag (success set to 0), so only runs that already failed and warned are affected; cache_fit_res still records the raw solver output.

Regression test test_solve_power_no_solution_returns_nan uses TTestPower with effect_size=0.5 and alternative='smaller', and effect_size=-0.5 with alternative='larger', expecting ConvergenceWarning, nan result and cache_fit_res[0] == 0; a solvable control case effect_size=0.5 with alternative='larger' must return a finite value.

Reproduction example: TTestPower().solve_power(effect_size=0.5, alpha=0.05, power=0.8, alternative='smaller') emits ConvergenceWarning 'Failed to converge on a solution.' and previously returned array([10.]).
Passages do not state the initialisation, the stopping criterion, the root-finder tolerance, or the iteration count at which behaviour differs.
reproduction_risks: Passages do not give the solver tolerance or iteration limit, so a reproduction cannot be checked against a specific convergence threshold.
Bracket bound value of 10 is specific to the cited example and may not generalise across inputs.
A follow-up (#9885) changed the ConvergenceWarning message to include the last evaluated value; reproduction matching on warning text may differ.
